plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating sp3d hybridization in phosphorus pentachloride (PCl5) at the molecular and orbital levels. Panel (a) shows a ball-and-stick model of PCl5 with an orange phosphorus atom at the center covalently bonded to five green chlorine atoms directed toward the vertices of a trigonal bipyramid: two axial Cl atoms situated above and below the central P atom along a vertical axis, and three equatorial Cl atoms arranged symmetrically in the horizontal plane. Panel (b) depicts the five sp3d hybrid orbitals that account for these five bonds, each shown as a large orange lobe radiating from a central black dot representing the phosphorus nucleus, labeled "sp3d," and arranged in the same trigonal bipyramidal pattern with dashed lines connecting the lobe tips to outline the geometry; small back-lobes are omitted for clarity. This figure establishes sp3d hybridization — derived from mixing one 3s, three 3p, and one 3d orbital of phosphorus — as the valence-bond explanation for the five equivalent bonding regions in PCl5 and connects orbital theory directly to the observed trigonal bipyramidal molecular structure.

elements: two axial green chlorine spheres, one directly above and one directly below P along the vertical axis
three equatorial green chlorine spheres arranged 120° apart in the horizontal plane through P
five cylindrical bonds (half orange near P, half green near Cl) connecting P to each Cl
five orange sp3d hybrid orbital lobes radiating from a central black nucleus dot, pointing along the same five bond directions (two axial, three equatorial)
central black dot representing the phosphorus nucleus in the orbital view
dashed lines connecting the lobe tips outlining the trigonal bipyramid

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Switching between the physical ball-and-stick molecule and the hybrid orbital picture shows that the five sp3d lobes point along exactly the same five bond directions — orbital theory reproducing the observed geometry

Selecting one orbital lobe (or one Cl atom in model view) highlights both that lobe and its corresponding bond in the other view, making the one-to-one mapping between each hybrid orbital and each P–Cl bond explicit

Rotating the structure reveals that the three equatorial directions lie in one plane 120° apart while the two axial directions are collinear and perpendicular to that plane — the essence of trigonal bipyramidal geometry

demo_steps.title: Ball-and-stick model
demo_steps.narration: PCl5 as a physical model: orange P at the center, two axial Cl above and below, three equatorial Cl spaced 120° apart in the horizontal plane — five bonds toward the vertices of a trigonal bipyramid.

demo_steps.title: Hybrid orbital picture
demo_steps.narration: The same five directions, now shown as sp3d hybrid lobes radiating from the P nucleus, with dashed lines outlining the trigonal bipyramid. Each lobe overlaps a Cl orbital to form one bond.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Trigonal bipyramid centered at origin. Axial Cl at (0, ±2.4, 0); equatorial Cl at radius 2.0 in the XZ plane at azimuths 90°, 210°, 330° (so one equatorial bond points screen-right as in the source, and two point up-left/down-left toward the viewer side). Bond cylinders ~0.12 radius, split into orange half (from P) and green half (to Cl). P sphere radius ~0.5, orange #e8821e; Cl spheres radius ~0.55, green #3fae2a with darker green shading; bonds green-orange gradient halves as in source. Orbital view: five elongated teardrop lobes (large lobe only, back lobes omitted) along the identical five directions, length ~2.2 units, max radius ~0.7, semi-opaque orange #f0a13a; nucleus black sphere radius ~0.12; dashed grey-green lines connecting the five lobe tips (triangle among the three equatorial tips plus lines from each axial tip to each equatorial tip). Label each lobe 'sp3d'. Both views share the same origin and orientation so the toggle cross-fades without reorienting.
interactionPlan.notes: Keep both views in the scene and cross-fade visibility on the toggle so the shared trigonal bipyramidal skeleton is perceived as identical. Clicking a lobe in orbital view (or a Cl/bond in model view) sets a shared selectedDirection index (0-4); highlight that direction in BOTH views (emissive boost or outline on the lobe, its bond, and its Cl) so the mapping is visible after toggling. Raycast against lobes, Cl spheres, and bond cylinders. Labels 'sp3d' as sprites; hide all but the selected lobe's label if clutter is an issue, otherwise show all five as in the source.

authoredContext:
In a molecule of phosphorus pentachloride, PCl 5 , there are five P–Cl bonds (thus five pairs of valence electrons around the phosphorus atom) directed toward the corners of a trigonal bipyramid. We use the 3 s orbital, the three 3 p orbitals, and one of the 3 d orbitals to form the set of five sp 3 d hybrid orbitals ( ) that are involved in the P–Cl bonds. Other atoms that exhibit sp 3 d hybridization include the sulfur atom in SF 4 and the chlorine atoms in ClF 3 and in ClF 4 + . (The electrons on fluorine atoms are omitted for clarity.)

(a) The five regions of electron density around phosphorus in PCl 5 require five hybrid sp 3 d orbitals. (b) These orbitals combine to form a trigonal bipyramidal structure with each large lobe of the hybrid orbital pointing at a vertex. As before, there are also small lobes pointing in the opposite direction for each orbital (not shown for clarity).

Two images are shown and labeled “a” and “b.” Image a depicts a ball-and-stick model in a trigonal bipyramidal arrangement. Image b depicts the hybrid orbitals in the same arrangement and each is labeled, “s p superscript three d.”

The sulfur atom in sulfur hexafluoride, SF 6 , exhibits sp 3 d 2 hybridization. A molecule of sulfur hexafluoride has six bonding pairs of electrons connecting six fluorine atoms to a single sulfur atom. There are no lone pairs of electrons on the central atom. To bond six fluorine atoms, the 3 s orbital, the three 3 p orbitals, and two of the 3 d orbitals form six equivalent sp 3 d 2 hybrid orbitals, each directed toward a different corner of an octahedron. Other atoms that exhibit sp 3 d 2 hybridization include the phosphorus atom in PCl 6 − , the iodine atom in the interhalogens IF 6 + , IF 5 , ICl 4 − , IF 4 − and the xenon atom in XeF 4 .

discrepancies: Orbital view (part b) connects all pairs of lobe tips with dashed lines (a complete K5 graph) rather than just the trigonal-bipyramid edges shown in the source, adding spurious diagonal lines
Source orbital view shows dashed green arrows along each bond axis from the nucleus; the generated orbital view has only dashed edges and lobes, no axis arrows

Only one 'Cl' label is shown in the model view, while the source leaves atoms unlabeled; the floating sp³d labels in model view appear as stray text near atoms before the toggle is used (visible in screenshot as tiny marks)
The source's small arrows inside the lobes indicating hybridization direction are absent
evaluation.notes: Faithful trigonal-bipyramidal PCl5 ball-and-stick model with a well-implemented toggle to the sp³d hybrid orbital view and useful click-to-highlight cross-view linking; minor extras (K5 dashed edges, missing axis arrows) keep it from perfect fidelity.
action_items: Limit the dashed lines in the orbital view to the trigonal-bipyramid edges (3 equatorial ring edges + 6 axial-to-equatorial edges) instead of connecting all tip pairs
Add dashed arrows from the nucleus along each of the five bond directions in the orbital view to match the source's axis arrows
Hide or reposition the sp³d labels when in ball-and-stick mode so they don't appear as stray text near the Cl atoms
